title: Evolution batch manifest (version 2)
description: The shape a freeze writes, and the only one this build reads. Version 2 adds the per-report cohort provenance invariants 4 and 5 need, and the batch base every experiment starts from. Version 1 was dropped rather than kept as a frozen reader schema: no batch has ever been frozen, so there is no immutable manifest at that version to keep readable. That window closes at the first successful freeze — after it, a frozen manifest cannot be migrated and its schema has to stay.

runner_protocol_revision.description: This batch's base: where the configured source line ([source_line].ref) stood when the batch was formed, as a full commit id. One commit under two readings — the stable protocol revision governing this cohort's evolution tasks (contract invariant 8), and the commit every experiment of this batch starts from (invariant 15). Required and never null: the line is what selects the batch's members, so a checkout that cannot resolve it refuses to freeze rather than record the absence. Not a release tag and not the per-report `provenance.runner_protocol_revision`, which is the revision a report's own runs were produced under.

selection.description: This batch's own denominator: what was considered when it was formed, how it split, and why each considered task that is not a member was left out. Membership is equality of deployable canonical identity against `runner_protocol_revision` (contract invariants 1 and 5), decided per unique completed task over every report that task owns, against the pending pool as it stood at formation. Recorded here because the pool is ignored machine-local state that moves: without it a frozen manifest reads as if the pool held exactly its members, and a cohort's recurrence claim is about the set it was drawn from. The agreement between these counts and the reports below is a cross-field rule this schema cannot state; `manifests.require_coherent_selection` enforces it in both directions, and a manifest that contradicts itself is refused when it is read as well as when it is written.

considered.description: Unique completed tasks the formation answered for: the members plus every non-selection below.

auto_selected.description: Members the identity test selected. Stated apart from `human_included` and never summed with it: a batch of ten that is nine judgements and one qualifying report is a different document from a batch of ten.

human_included.description: Members a human argued in past the identity test — invariant 1's sanctioned exception, which counts toward the batch thresholds like any other member and is recorded with its justification and actor on each of its reports.

not_selected.description: Every considered task that is not a member, with the reason. Kept as records rather than as a count so the reasons stay distinguishable: `identity-differs` and `revision-absent` are facts about the evidence, `revision-malformed` is a fact about the record, `revision-unresolvable` is a fact about the clone that formed the batch, and `human-excluded` is a judgement somebody made and is named for.

items.description: One report's membership entry. Identity and content hash pin what was analyzed; evaluator and provenance carry the cohort-coherence facts (contract invariants 4 and 5) so a frozen batch answers 'is this one cohort?' from committed content alone, without the ignored raw bundles.

selection.description: How this report's task came to be a member. Membership is decided per unique completed task (invariant 1), and this is the report that decision was taken over: a task's evidence is its one latest evaluation, so the identity test and the manifest read the same report and no report is marked automatic on another report's evidence. Carried on the report so an entry read on its own says why it is in the batch.

justification.description: Why a human moved this task in, in their own words. Null for `auto`: an automatic member records no judgement, and words there would read as one that was never made. The same field names a human exclusion's reason, so the two directions of one window are read the same way.

not_selected.description: One considered task left out of the batch, and why.

justification.description: Why a human took this task out, in their own words. Null for every machine reason, which is already its own explanation. Stated because an exclusion removes evidence the identity test had selected — the move most able to shape what a cohort says, and so the one least able to go unexplained.
